content:
The S&P 500 closed lower on Tuesday after a broad sell-off, with the index falling well below its prior record high. Wide participation across sectors drove the decline, and heavy volume confirmed the move.

Global bond yields are falling, not rising. The U.S. 30-year Treasury yield has dropped to 4.85%, and French and U.K. 10-year yields have both declined.

The Reserve Bank of India cut rates by 25 basis points to 5.0% to support growth. Bank of Japan Governor Ueda's latest comments were more hawkish than expected, which is a headwind for the carry trade.

Investors are watching a $25 billion 10-year Treasury auction and the FOMC minutes, due at 4pm ET. Crude inventories showed a 1.2 million barrel build, and bitcoin is seeing buying.

The author of this piece is an external contributor. Benzinga states that it does not represent its own reporting and has not been edited for accuracy.
headline: Stocks Slide as Bond Yields Fall; Smaller Treasury Auction Ahead
summary: The S&P 500 fell on broad selling as bond yields dropped, with a smaller $25 billion Treasury auction and a surprise RBI rate cut ahead.
